question: Which delay in the three delays model does an emergency maternal transport scheme directly address?

options.A: The delay in diagnosing pregnancy complications
options.B: The delay in receiving treatment at the hospital
options.C: The delay in reaching a health facility
options.D: The delay in deciding to seek care

explanation: Transport schemes focus entirely on moving the patient physically from the community to a referral center, solving the second delay. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is a referral hospital often useless during a severe postpartum hemorrhage if transport is lacking?

options.A: Primary health centers have more blood than tertiary hospitals
options.B: The patient cannot receive life-saving care if she remains stuck in her remote village
options.C: Local midwives are banned from treating bleeding outside hospitals
options.D: Hospitals refuse to treat patients who arrive late from rural areas

explanation: No matter how advanced the hospital care is, it cannot help a woman who is physically unable to reach it in time. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is a common physical obstacle to maternal transport during the rainy season in rural areas?

options.C: Lack of fuel stations in major cities

explanation: Seasonal rains wash out unpaved rural paths, making standard cars unable to reach pregnant women in labor. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h2)

question: A remote community wants to prepare for transport emergencies during rainy months when cars cannot enter. What vehicle choice makes the most practical sense?

options.C: Locally adapted tricycles or modified motorcycles

explanation: Tricycles and modified motorcycles navigate narrow, muddy paths much better than large cars or buses. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why do transport schemes usually fail when they are completely organized by external agencies without local input?

options.A: External agencies always bring vehicles that are too modern to maintain
options.B: The community members do not feel a sense of ownership or trust in the system
options.C: Local governments forbid outsiders from entering rural settlements
options.D: Villagers prefer walking to hospitals rather than using vehicles

explanation: Involving locals in planning ensures the system fits their culture and needs, building the trust required for actual use. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h3)

question: Name a practical method for sensitizing a rural community to maternal transport needs.

options.A: Hosting town hall meetings and drama performances
options.B: Publishing academic journals in foreign countries
options.C: Sending formal letters to political leaders
options.D: Distributing social media ads on smartphones

explanation: Public gatherings and local drama groups effectively reach rural populations who rely on oral communication. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a community-based transport fund?

options.A: To generate heavy commercial profits for the village leadership
options.B: To purchase luxury vehicles for local chiefs
options.C: To remove sudden out-of-pocket cash demands during a medical emergency
options.D: To pay salaries for national government health ministers

explanation: Pooling funds beforehand ensures that lack of cash at midnight does not delay a woman's trip to the hospital. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h4)

question: How do micro-insurance models typically sustain emergency transport systems in villages?

options.A: Drivers give free rides and collect money later from international banks
options.B: Families contribute small, regular amounts so funds are ready before a crisis happens
options.C: Traditional rulers sell community land whenever a woman goes into labor
options.D: The government pays all transport costs retroactively at the end of the year

explanation: Small, steady contributions build a reliable financial pool without placing an unbearable burden on any single family. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why is it dangerous to ignore or sideline Traditional Birth Attendants when setting up a transport scheme?

options.A: They may delay referrals because they feel threatened, keeping complicated cases at home
options.B: They control all the financial wealth and vehicles in the community
options.C: They will refuse to let ambulances pass through village roads
options.D: They are legally certified to perform major cesarean sections

explanation: If TBAs feel respected and involved as partners, they will call for transport early instead of hiding complications. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h5)

question: What specific role should trained Traditional Birth Attendants play in an emergency transport system?

options.A: Performing emergency surgical procedures inside village huts
options.B: Spotting danger signs early and triggering the transport system without delay
options.C: Driving the emergency ambulance vehicles across highways at night
options.D: Managing the financial bank accounts of the local government

explanation: TBAs see women first; teaching them to recognize danger signs helps activate transport before it is too late. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is a major threat to the long-term survival of a community transport scheme?

options.A: Too many healthy mothers giving birth without problems
options.B: Lack of vehicle maintenance and financial transparency
options.C: Excessive availability of paved roads and fuel
options.D: Too many trained drivers wanting to help

explanation: Without regular vehicle servicing and honest money management, schemes quickly collapse from breakdowns and mistrust. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why are regular public auditing meetings essential for keeping a transport scheme running for years?

options.A: It prevents pregnant women from delivering babies at home
options.B: Drivers need public praise to drive faster during emergencies
options.C: Showing people how money is spent maintains trust and encourages continued donations
options.D: The government requires strict tax payments from village transport pools

explanation: Transparency proves that committee members are not stealing funds, keeping the community willing to pay into the system. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T4#BMP215_U3_T4_h6)
